messages:
alex: Heads-up — urgent from BetaCorp. They integrated embeddings with our TypeScript SDK and started sending batched requests. Intermittent 400s complaining about "dimension mismatch" and occasional 504 timeouts on retries. They say single-item calls always succeed.

priya: Can you paste the exact error payload and example request? Is this coming back from our backend or from the SDK validation?

alex: Customer logs:```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 1024 at input index 5"}
TS SDK v2.0.1 stack:
  at EmbeddingsClient.create (node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.js:432:22)
  at userService.ts:45:13
```
They also included a minimal repro in JS (they switched from small-embed -> large-embed recently):```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const texts = Array.from({length:8}, (_,i) => 'sentence ' + i);
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'open-embedder-large', input: texts, batchSize: 8 })
```

noah: Likely cause: mixing model variants in a single batch or a runtime change doing per-item routing. Any recent routing canary? ops-bot: reply?

ops-bot: Canary deployment: embed-routing v2.1 -> v2.2 started 2026-10-06T09:11:03Z. Traffic slice: 15% in eu-west1.

priya: If some items are routed to a 1024-d variant and others to 1536-d, the runtime should reject earlier. Do they use any caching layer returning precomputed vectors?

alex: They said they have a small local LRU cache of precomputed embeddings (from previous model) and are concatenating cached vectors with fresh text for batching. But they also said batch_size=1 always works. When batchSize >=4 they see failures.

rachel: Ask them to: 1) run batchSize=1 and confirm success (done), 2) enable RW_DEBUG=trace and share logs (asked), 3) pin exact variant name like open-embedder-large-v3 and retry. Also ask them to include headers X-RW-Model and X-RW-Variant if present.

alex: They sent trace. Key excerpts:```
[trace] client: request /v1/embeddings model=open-embedder-large batch=8
[trace] runtime: resolved target open-embedder-large-v3 (dim=1536)
[trace] runtime: fallback for item 5 -> open-embedder-medium-v2 (dim=1024) due to node load
[warn] runtime: mixed-dim batch detected, forwarding to execution
[error] api: 400 {"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 1024 at input index 5"}
```

noah: That looks like a regression where fallback selection is done per-item. We only allow request-level routing for embeddings. This is similar to past bug where sharder returned per-chunk mapping. I'll open an eng-runtime ticket.

priya: Short-term mitigations for the customer: set batchSize=1, pin model to variant name, and upgrade SDK — we have a client-side guard in TS SDK v2.0.2 that rejects mixed-dim inputs before sending. Also advise exponential backoff on retries, not tight immediate retries.

alex: Customer also reported a billing "401" briefly after a flurry of retries. billing-bot, can you check if retries could have caused a transient auth token rotation or duplicate charge window?

billing-bot: Observed token refresh events at 2026-10-06T09:13:21Z for BetaCorp org; 3 retry attempts between 09:13:20-09:13:25Z. No duplicate charges detected in ledger, but there were two failed invoice attempts due to transient auth failure; cleared automatically. Recommend client use idempotency keys and backoff.

rachel: Action plan: (1) Ops rollback canary routing slice immediately. (2) Hotfix: runtime should validate that all resolved targets for a single embeddings request share identical dimension before sending them for execution and fail fast with a clearer error code bad_request.mixed_dimensions. (3) Ship TS SDK v2.0.2 with pre-send dim check + safer default retry (exp backoff with jitter). (4) Provide BetaCorp a patched client if they can't upgrade.

noah: I'll start the rollback. Also adding a unit test that simulates node-level fallback to smaller-variant and asserts we reject at route time.

ops-bot: Rollback started: embed-routing v2.2 -> v2.1 at 2026-10-06T09:27:12Z. Monitoring 10m.

alex: BetaCorp asked for repro steps they can run to validate after we fix. Suggested snippet I gave them (TS):```bash
export RW_DEBUG=trace
node -e "const R=require('@redwood/sdk');const c=new R.Redwood();const texts=Array.from({length:8},(_,i)=>'x'.repeat(i+1));c.embeddings.create({model:'open-embedder-large',input:texts,batchSize:8}).then(console.log).catch(console.error)"
```

priya: Also send them a Go example demonstrating safe batching (v0.9.1 patch) and how to set idempotency key and retry policy. Example:```go
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("RW_KEY"))
opts := redwood.EmbeddingsOptions{Model: "open-embedder-large-v3", BatchSize: 4, RetryPolicy: redwood.ExponentialBackoff(100*time.Millisecond, 3)}
resp, err := client.Embeddings.Create(ctx, inputs, opts)
```

alex: Customer accepted workaround (batchSize=1 + pin variant) and asked us to notify when rollback is complete or patch deployed. I'll update them.

rachel: After rollback, we should run a chaos test that randomly makes per-item routing plausible and ensure server rejects mixed-dim batches. Also audit other endpoints for similar per-item routing regressions.

noah: Filed ENG-RUNTIME-4589 and assigned to @rachel and @manu. ETA for hotfix: 3 hours for server-side guard + tests, deploy in next patch. SDK patch release ETA: 6 hours for TS/Go.

alex: Thanks. I'll keep thread updated. :raised_hands:

ops-bot: Rollback complete at 2026-10-06T09:36:45Z. Canary reverted, monitoring stable.
